text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Council of Europe rapporteur on Cyprus says all those missing since 1974 are dead. "There is no logic in the policies of Cypriots - in the end both communities will pay," he says.
- Small shareholders in Hellenic Chemical Companies demand their money back, claiming the company decieved them.
- Annual Nikiforos military exercise starts today.
- Council of Europe rapporteur warns of punitive action against both sides in Cyprus if talks fail.
- New House of Representatives session to face a deluge of new bills.
- Mediation service at the Labour Ministry spends half its time addressing disputes at Cyprus Airways
- History vindicated communist Akel, says its chief Demetris Christofias.
- The rift in conservative Democratic Rally deepens after comments by its MP Katy Clerides that it has ceased being a progressive party of the right.
- Council of Europe rapporteur criticises President Glafcos Clerides's handling of the Cyprus problem in report.
- Greece will have a stronger presence in Cypriot military exercise which starts today.
- Foreigners living in Limassol, Paphos and other areas have turned their neighbourhoods into little ghettos.
- Council of Europe rapporteur on Cyprus will invite Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash to a joint meeting.
- Employers and trade unions are on a collision course over productivity levels.
